patch.value: A same-day re-release is blocked because the pinned pm-changelog rejects the -N version suffix

The release job failed at Generate changelog and release notes with "--date-from-version requires a calendar version in YYYY.M.D form; received 2026.9.6-1", so nothing was published and npm stayed on the previous version.

The version scheme appends a -N suffix when a release already exists for the same calendar day, which is exactly what a second release on one day produces. pm-changelog 2026.8.17, the version this repository had installed, rejects that suffix. pm-changelog 2026.9.2 accepts it: its own error text reads "optionally with a same-day -N suffix", and running it here with --release-version 2026.9.6-1 --date-from-version exits 0 and writes the file, where 2026.8.17 exits 1.

So this is a stale dependency rather than a defect in either package. The declared range was already ^2026.8.17, which would resolve to 2026.9.2 on a fresh install, but CI runs npm ci and the lockfile pinned 2026.8.17. The declared range is not the binding constraint; the lockfile is.

Worth recording because of how it surfaced. The release completeness audit had never executed - its gh calls carried no token - so the release job had reported failure on eight consecutive runs while publishing successfully. Giving that step its token made the job's status meaningful again, and the very next run surfaced this genuine blocker before publishing rather than after. A permanently red job cannot report a new failure; that is the whole cost of leaving one red.
Bumped pm-changelog to 2026.9.2, which accepts a same-day -N suffix on the calendar version.
A second release on one calendar day generates its changelog from the suffixed version and publishes.
The pinned 2026.8.17 rejected 2026.9.6-1, so the job failed before publishing and npm stayed on the previous version.
Bumped pm-changelog to 2026.9.2, which accepts a same-day -N suffix on the calendar version.
